spec_features.spec_quote: early-stop once a spiral is unambiguous
spec_features.evidence: loop.py:135-144 checks `if harness_cfg.early_stop_on_spiral and detector.fired` then counts down grace_left and sets terminal_reason='early_stop' + break. It is genuinely wired and breaks the loop, but `early_stop_on_spiral` defaults False (config.py:51) and is only on when --early-stop passed (runner.py:55).
spec_features.notes: Detector requires dup-action window AND self-crit conjunction (detector.py); only fires on narrow trigger and is off in canonical mode.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Off for canonical scoring to avoid biasing severity (DESIGN 2.5 / 6).

spec_features.spec_quote: spiral-triggered early stop** that records the turn index at which the spiral became unambiguous
spec_features.evidence: detector.py records `_fired_turn` exposed as onset_turn; loop.py:147 stores tr.oracle['detector_onset_turn']=detector.onset_turn and the early_stop break at loop.py:143-144 honors it. Same mechanism as above, off by default.
spec_features.notes: Onset turn always recorded; the halt only fires when early_stop_on_spiral enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Once a spiral is unmistakable ... record the turn index ... time-to-spiral (detector.py docstring, instrumental metric)

spec_features.evidence: loop.py: `for step in range(harness_cfg.max_steps)` bounds the loop; submit handled via dispatch outcome.submitted -> submitted_summary, loop.py:131 sets terminal_reason='submit' and break; fallthrough sets terminal_reason='max_steps' at loop.py:148. tools.py:submit handler returns submitted=True.
config.py:48 `max_steps: int = 18`; loop.py: `for step in range(harness_cfg.max_steps)` actually bounds the loop and forces stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: max_steps: int = 18  # ReAct turns before forced stop

spec_features.spec_quote: Spiral early-stop** (screening mode): stop K=3 turns after the spiral detector first fires
spec_features.evidence: config.py:52 early_stop_grace_turns=3; loop.py:136-144 sets grace_left=early_stop_grace_turns on first fire then decrements and breaks at grace_left<=0. Wired and enforced only when early_stop_on_spiral=True (default False).
spec_features.notes: Grace countdown works but gated behind the off-by-default screening flag.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: early_stop_grace_turns: int = 3      # confirm K turns after detector fires

spec_features.evidence: base.py:69-73: if amp.permission_to_stop, appends real instruction text 'you may call `submit` with a clear explanation of the blocker instead.' wired via runner.py:64 from --permission-to-stop. The referenced submit tool is fully built/honored (tools.py, loop.py). HONEST_BLOCKER control hard-codes the permission text regardless of the flag (honest_blocker.py system_prompt).
spec_features.notes: Real exit text delivered and submit honored as stop; but it is only a prompt nudge (default permission_to_stop=False) — the subject must still choose submit; no code forces an exit on distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: permission_to_stop: bool = False     # explicit "you may declare blocked" (control arm: should reduce spirals)

spec_features.spec_quote: Resource caps: per-command wall-clock timeout, output byte cap, max file size, max total commands.
spec_features.evidence: sandbox.py: subprocess.run timeout=per_command_timeout_s with TimeoutExpired -> exit 124; _trunc enforces max_output_bytes; read_file/write_file raise on >max_file_bytes; run_command checks `if self._commands_run >= self.cfg.max_total_commands: return budget exhausted` and increments counter. All four caps are read and enforced.
spec_features.notes: All four resource caps enforced end-to-end against the sandbox.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Defensive — these tasks invite runaway loops (DESIGN); code comment: 'hard runaway guard across the run'
